newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil's share as primary energy source dips in FY95.
newsitem.headline: Oil's share as primary energy source dips in FY95.

text.p: Japan's dependence on crude oil as a source of primary energy declined for the first time in almost 30 years in fiscal 1995/96, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Friday.
It said crude accounted for 55.8 percent of Japan's primary energy sources, down from 57.4 percent the year before.
MITI attributed the decline largely to a sharp drop in crude oil demand among electric utilities, which led to a dip in crude imports.
Crude oil was still the largest source of primary energy, followed by coal at 16.5 percent, nuclear energy at 12 percent and natural gas at 10.8 percent, it said.

Final energy consumption in fiscal 1995/96 rose 3.2 percent from the year before, the second successive year that consumption has risen more than three percent. Final energy consumption includes all sources of energy such as electricity, gas and oil products.
The rise in final energy consumption surpasses earlier forecasts, which predicted an average year-on-year climb of one percent from fiscal 1992/93 to fiscal 2000/2001, MITI said.
